```{r setup}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(DT)

store_path <- if (dir.exists("_targets")) "_targets" else
  file.path(here::here(), "docs/_targets")
tar_config_set(store = store_path)

utils_path <- if (file.exists("vignette_utils.R")) "vignette_utils.R" else
  file.path(here::here(), "docs/vignette_utils.R")
source(utils_path)

jst_equity_premium <- safe_tar_read("jst_equity_premium")
jst_pervasiveness  <- safe_tar_read("jst_pervasiveness")
jst_crises         <- safe_tar_read("jst_crises")
jst_summary        <- safe_tar_read("jst_summary")
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Negative Results

Negative results now live in one place: the **[Failed and Watch Strategies](failures.html)** page. It lists every strategy whose computed verdict is not Keep, with the failing test, the key metrics, the written reason, the date and the issue link. The verdict is derived from the leaderboard and falsification numbers, so it cannot drift from them the way the hand-written cards that used to sit here did.

- Why each strategy is ranked where it is: [Strategy Leaderboard](leaderboard.html)
- The alpha test behind the "no alpha" verdicts: [Strategy Falsification](falsification.html)
- Avoid Worst Days analysis: [avoid-worst-days.html](avoid-worst-days.html)

The long-run historical evidence on the equity premium stays on the next tab.

## Historical Evidence {#historical-evidence}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Overview

The [Jordà-Schularick-Taylor Macrohistory Database](https://www.macrohistory.net/database/){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"} provides 150+ years of macroeconomic and financial data across `r jst_summary$n_countries` advanced economies, spanning `r jst_summary$year_range[1]` to `r jst_summary$year_range[2]`. This tab analyzes the equity premium (equity total return minus short-term government bill rate) to test the cross-geography pervasiveness criterion from the Swedroe evidence-based investing framework.

**Key findings:**

- Equity premium is positive in `r jst_summary$pervasive_count` of `r jst_summary$pervasive_total` countries over the full sample (mean > 0, t-stat > 2, majority of years positive)
- Financial crises occurred in `r nrow(jst_crises)` countries, with total crisis-years ranging from `r min(jst_crises$n_crises)` to `r max(jst_crises$n_crises)` per country

**Source:** Òscar Jordà, Moritz Schularick, and Alan M. Taylor (2017). "Macrofinancial History and the New Business Cycle Facts." In *NBER Macroeconomics Annual 2016*, volume 31, edited by Martin Eichenbaum and Jonathan A. Parker. Chicago: University of Chicago Press. [DOI: 10.1086/690241](https://doi.org/10.1086/690241){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"}

### Cross-Geography Pervasiveness

The table below shows full-sample equity premium statistics by country, sorted by mean premium. A factor is considered *pervasive* if it has a positive mean premium, t-statistic > 2, and is positive in more than 50% of years.

```{r jst-pervasiveness}
#| label: jst-pervasiveness
#| tbl-cap: "Equity premium pervasiveness test: full-sample statistics by country. Countries are sorted by mean premium. The 'Pervasive' column indicates whether the premium meets all three criteria: positive mean, t-stat > 2, and positive in >50% of years. Data source: <a href=\"https://www.macrohistory.net/database/\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">JST Macrohistory Database</a>."

jst_pervasiveness |>
  select(
    Country = iso,
    Period = from_year,
    `To Year` = to_year,
    `N Years` = n_years,
    `Mean (%)` = mean_premium,
    `SD (%)` = sd_premium,
    `t-stat` = t_stat,
    `% Positive` = pct_positive,
    Pervasive = pervasive
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 2))) |>
  datatable(
    options = list(
      pageLength = 20,
      dom = 't',
      columnDefs = list(
        list(className = 'dt-center', targets = 1:8)
      )
    ),
    rownames = FALSE
  ) |>
  formatStyle(
    'Mean (%)',
    background = styleColorBar(range(jst_pervasiveness$mean_premium, na.rm = TRUE), '#69d4a0'),
    backgroundSize = '100% 90%',
    backgroundRepeat = 'no-repeat',
    backgroundPosition = 'center'
  ) |>
  formatStyle(
    'Pervasive',
    backgroundColor = styleEqual(c(TRUE, FALSE), c('#69d4a0', '#555555'))
  )
```

### Visualisations

The two static figures below (heatmap, crisis timeline) are grouped into tabs to shorten this section further. Earlier revisions of this page kept the JST data tables outside any tab, citing a known defect class where a `DT::datatable()` table can measure zero height if its tab starts inactive. That risk has since been checked directly against this page's rendered HTML: the JST pervasiveness and crisis-frequency tables both carry their full row counts while sitting in an inactive tab, so the tables in this section are now nested in tabs like everything else.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Equity Premium Heatmap

The heatmap below shows mean equity premium by decade and country. Darker green indicates higher premium; red indicates negative premium. Missing cells represent periods with insufficient data.

```{r jst-heatmap}
#| label: jst-heatmap
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Equity premium heatmap: mean excess return (equity total return minus bill rate) by decade and country, ", jst_summary$year_range[1], "-", jst_summary$year_range[2], ". Green shades indicate positive premium, red indicates negative. Data source: <a href=\"https://www.macrohistory.net/database/\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">JST Macrohistory Database</a>. Generated by <a href=\"https://github.com/JohnGavin/historical/blob/main/R/plan_jst.R#L13\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">R/plan_jst.R</a>.")'
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8

ggplot(jst_equity_premium, aes(x = decade, y = iso, fill = mean_premium)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#f08080",
    mid = "#1a1a2e",
    high = "#69d4a0",
    midpoint = 0,
    na.value = "grey50",
    name = "Mean Premium (%)"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1870, 2020, 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Equity Premium by Decade and Country",
    subtitle = paste0(jst_summary$year_range[1], "-", jst_summary$year_range[2]),
    x = "Decade",
    y = "Country"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "grey60"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

#### Financial Crisis Timeline

Financial crises (identified by the JST `crisisJST` indicator) are shown below as segments spanning crisis years for each country.

```{r jst-crises-timeline}
#| label: jst-crises-timeline
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Financial crisis timeline: crisis years by country, ", jst_summary$year_range[1], "-", jst_summary$year_range[2], ". Each segment represents a crisis year as identified by the JST crisisJST indicator. Data source: <a href=\"https://www.macrohistory.net/database/\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">JST Macrohistory Database</a>.")'
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6

crises_long <- jst_crises |>
  separate_rows(crisis_years, sep = ", ") |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(crisis_years)) |>
  select(iso, year) |>
  arrange(iso, year)

ggplot(crises_long, aes(x = year, y = iso)) +
  geom_point(color = "#f08080", size = 2) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(xend = year + 1, yend = iso),
    color = "#f08080",
    linewidth = 1,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1870, 2020, 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Financial Crisis Timeline",
    subtitle = paste0(jst_summary$year_range[1], "-", jst_summary$year_range[2]),
    x = "Year",
    y = "Country"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "grey60")
  )
```

:::

### Crisis Frequency Table

The table below shows the number of crisis years per country, sorted by total crisis-years.

```{r jst-crises-table}
#| label: jst-crises-table
#| tbl-cap: "Financial crisis frequency by country: total crisis-years identified by the JST crisisJST indicator. Countries are sorted by total crisis count. Data source: <a href=\"https://www.macrohistory.net/database/\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">JST Macrohistory Database</a>."

jst_crises |>
  select(
    Country = iso,
    `Total Crisis Years` = n_crises,
    `Crisis Years` = crisis_years
  ) |>
  datatable(
    options = list(
      pageLength = 20,
      dom = 't',
      columnDefs = list(
        list(className = 'dt-center', targets = 1)
      )
    ),
    rownames = FALSE
  ) |>
  formatStyle(
    'Total Crisis Years',
    background = styleColorBar(range(jst_crises$n_crises), '#f08080'),
    backgroundSize = '100% 90%',
    backgroundRepeat = 'no-repeat',
    backgroundPosition = 'center'
  )
```

### Data Notes

- **Equity premium** = equity total return (`eq_tr`) - short-term government bill rate (`bill_rate`)
- **Pervasiveness criteria**: mean premium > 0, t-stat > 2, and positive in >50% of years
- **Crisis indicator**: `crisisJST` binary flag (1 = crisis year)
- **Country coverage**: `r jst_summary$n_countries` countries: `r paste(sort(unique(jst_pervasiveness$iso)), collapse = ", ")`
- **Data period**: `r jst_summary$year_range[1]` to `r jst_summary$year_range[2]` (`r format(jst_summary$n_obs, big.mark = ",")` country-year observations)

All target computations are defined in [`R/plan_jst.R`](https://github.com/JohnGavin/historical/blob/main/R/plan_jst.R#L13).

## Related vignettes

- **[Falsification](falsification.html)** — applies formal hypothesis testing to each strategy's conditional independence claims; the long-run JST evidence is a key input to those priors
- **[Strategy Leaderboard](leaderboard.html)** — ranks all strategies on risk-adjusted return; the equity premium evidence here contextualises what "good" looks like across 100+ years
- **[Factor MAX](stock-backtest.html#factor-level-deep-dive)** — applies cross-sectional factor rotation to the same academic factors whose long-run premia are documented in the JST data
- **[Negative Results](failures.html)** — strategies that failed to survive empirical scrutiny; the historical evidence framework here explains why they were rejected
